name: Lavatbura-Lamusong
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only 1876 wordlists (Strauch) and Ross 1988 comparative; no grammar/phonology exists

sources.citation: Du, Jingyi. 2010. Towards a grammar of the Usen dialect of the Barok language, New Ireland. PhD thesis, La Trobe University.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Sister language (Barok) only: primary stress on the final syllable (sec. 2.9, pp. 56-58). Lamasong mentioned only as a Madak-chain member (p. ~7) and via Ross 1994: 558-559 (shared intervocalic lenition). No lbv stress statement.

sources.citation: Lindström, Eva. 2002. Topics in the grammar of Kuot, a non-Austronesian language of New Ireland. PhD thesis, Stockholm University. Ch. 3 Phonology.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Sec. 3.10 Areal phonology (pp. 127-128): features Kuot shares with Lamasong/Madak/Barok are lenition of intervocalic voiceless stops, no final voiced stops, final l > n, weak schwa/a opposition; stress is not among them. Cites Ross 1994 for a Madak-chain language-shift scenario.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page lava1239 (refs: Ross 1988: 257-314; Ross 1994; Strauch 1876 x2)
sources.note: Bibliographic page only; lists no grammar or phonology for the language (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Lamasong appears in the consonant-correspondence Table 34 (pp. 266-268), sec. 8.6.3 'The Madak chain' (p. 292) and morphosyntactic comparisons; informant Benson Berom of Lamasong (App. A), Clay 1977 as other source (App. B); fn. 10 p. 413 notes Kuot phonotactic influence on Madak and Lamasong (citing Ross 1981c). No statement on stress or accent for Lamasong anywhere (all 'stress' hits concern other languages).

sources.citation: Beaumont, Clive H. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study vol. 2, Pacific Linguistics C-39: 387-397.
sources.note: Classification and sound-correspondence notes (Lavatbura-Lamusong reflexes of *q etc.); no mention of stress, accent or suprasegmentals.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.citation: Beaumont, Clive H. 1972. New Ireland languages: a review. Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3, Pacific Linguistics A-35: 1-41.
sources.note: Sec. 1.4 Phonology (pp. 20-22) is a phonetic-level survey of all New Ireland languages; Lavatbura-Lamusong named only for reported ! and z (p. 21); sec. 1.4.9 Tone reports tone only for Kara, Barok and Sokirik Patpatar. The word 'stress' occurs only for Tigak (Beaumont 1969). Nothing on lbv stress.
sources.venue: Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3, Pacific Linguistics A-35: 1-41

sources.citation: Strauch, H. 1876. Verzeichniss von 477 Wörtern, gesammelt während des Aufenthaltes S.M.S. 'Gazelle' in Neu-Guinea, Neu-Hannover, Neu-Irland, Neu-Britannien und Brisbane (Queensland). Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 8: 405-420.
sources.note: Comparative wordlist; column 'IV. Neu-Irland. 2. Ankerplatz' (3°11.5'S 151°39.3'E, 4-6 Aug 1875) is the lbv material per Glottolog. The introduction (pp. 405-406) says nothing about accent/Betonung; Google-scan scanned garbles the diacritics on the words, so no accent placement can be read from it.

sources.citation: Strauch, H. 1876. Verzeichniss von 477 Wörtern.. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 8: 405-420 (better scan needed; archive.org Google scan scanned garbles diacritics).
sources.note: Only 19th-century lbv data; a clean scan (BHL/HathiTrust) would show whether the collector marked accent on the Neu-Irland 2. Ankerplatz words, though it would still be data rather than a statement.

sources.citation: Mazzitelli, Lidia Federica & Edelvina Turughai (eds.). 2026. È ra pinara ngàn kalanu: Lamasong Story Book. (Lamasong Reader Series 1.) Kalispell, Montana: Education Projects International. 86 pp. (ISBN as printed 9-798895-913574.) Open copy: Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.18888217 (concept doi 10.5281/zenodo.18888216; Zenodo creators listed as Turughai, Edelvina; Mazzitelli, Lidia Federica; language lbv; CC-BY 4.0; published 2026-03-06).

tone.quote: In this book, Lamasong is written with 8 vowels and 18 consonants. [...] Because Lamasong has more sounds than there are letters in the English or Tok Pisin alphabets, the spelling in this book uses five special letters: the vowels à, è, é, ò and ó. Most letters are pronounced as in Tok Pisin. There are some differences, which do not exist in Tok Pisin: à is pronounced [ə], as in English about.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
